description:
A bare control-flow statement after DECLARED prose at a §40.8 body-top is code: it is checked (no diagnostic for `if (1) { }`) and never rendered; the declared

renders.
rationale: ⛑ S441 RE-AUTHORED — a `<program>` / `<page>` / `<channel>` body carries no loose prose (§40.8 S441 bullet; ruling user-voice-scrml.md S441 "prose should be declared as such" + "declared-prose implementation: yes to all four"). Pre-S441 this case pinned `if (1) { }` shipping into the page as text (the S378 hole). The body is code now, so the statement is parsed and not rendered. This case exists because the alternative is a normative row that says more than the compiler does — the exact Rule 4 defect that opened this arc. `SPEC.md` §34's E-CONTROL-FLOW-IN-MARKUP row lists a `<program>`/`<page>`/`<channel>` default-logic root under 'Does NOT fire', reason given, 'the §40.8 auto-lift handles it'. The 'does not fire' half is what this case pins. ⚑ THE REASON IS STILL FALSE and the case is the standing evidence: §40.8's own S123 amendment says the auto-lift covers DECLARATIONS ONLY, so the locus is covered by NEITHER the lift nor the error, and the construct ships as page text. ⚑ S383 — WHY THIS IS NOT SIMPLY FIXED. Ruling 3 (S375) directed exactly this extension and an implementation reached four review rounds; at S383 it was HELD, because the recognizer needs a `{` to tell code from prose — so `if (@a) log(1)` (braceless), `switch (@a) { }`, a labelled `for` and a `do { … } while (@a)` ALL ship raw into the DOM with zero diagnostics at BOTH loci, including the markup locus that has been shipping since S203. That is a permanent hole inside the class the diagnostic exists to close, and it needs a grammar-derived recognizer rather than another pattern. The full problem statement, the measured shapes, the cross-axis corpus and the safety property a successor owes are in `docs/changes/ruling3-grammar-derived/PROBLEM-STATEMENT.md`. ⚑ IF A RULING LATER LANDS THAT WORK, THIS CASE IS THE ONE TO FLIP, and flipping it should be a deliberate act with a ruling behind it rather than a silent green-to-green edit. Sibling pins: `ctrl-012-bare-control-flow-default-logic-root-neg` (the wrapped `${ ... }` form, correctly silent), `ctrl-012-default-logic-prose-neg` and `ctrl-012-default-logic-multiline-prose-neg` (prose, correctly silent — counter-gates against OVER-reaching), and `ctrl-012-bare-control-flow-in-markup-pos` (the S203 markup locus, where a BRACED statement does fire). MEASURED at this revision: zero errors and zero warnings, and the statement text appears in the emitted HTML. ⛑ THE `dom` ASSERTION IS WHAT MAKES THE OUTPUT CLAIM ENFORCED RATHER THAN NARRATED. This case's whole point is that the statement SHIPS AS PAGE TEXT, and a codes-only expectation cannot see that: a successor recognizer that applied the S203 reject-and-recover TEXT-DROP while emitting no diagnostic would delete `if (1) { }` from `<body>` and this case would stay green while silently changing what the compiler does. Whole-tree `dom` rather than `domAnchored` because the shipped statement is a BARE TEXT NODE directly under `<body>` with no wrapping element, so no selector reaches it — measured, `domAnchored` with `selector: "body"` reports 'no match' because the anchored root IS the body. ⛑ S383 (R3) — `notCodePrefixes` MAKES THE SILENCE CLAIM ENFORCED RATHER THAN NARRATED. `codes: []` asserts NOTHING: `run.ts:441` computes `missing` by filtering the LISTED codes, so an empty list can never be violated, and `notCodes` constrains exactly one code. This case says the compiler is silent here, so it now forbids the whole `E-` and `W-` families (`run.ts:446-450`). MEASURED before pinning, through the runner rather than by hand: with `E-`, `W-` AND `I-` all forbidden, this case reports ZERO prefix violations. `I-` is deliberately left unpinned — the advisory/lint stream is a separate partition (S92/S93) and may legitimately gain hints at this locus without that being a regression here.
